sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-End Loose-Leaf Tea Service and Cultural Ceramic Salons

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Alberta, Canada (Province of Alberta; corporate registry administered by Service Alberta)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal-Provincial constitutional monarchy; Alberta applies English-derived Common Law doctrine with stare decisis and statutory construction under the Interpretation Act, RSA 2000, c I-8)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended by Protocols including the Fifth Protocol (in force December 16, 2023) - recognizes Canadian unlimited liability corporations as hybrid entities
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 2012; in force 2014) - applicable to PRC-domiciled investors or upstream shareholders
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent BEPS (MLI) - in force for Canada as applicable to covered tax treaties
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA, in force July 1, 2020) - goods and services trade, including beverage service inputs
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU (provisional application since September 21, 2017) - relevant to EU-origin tea and ceramic imports
WTO General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS) - Mode 3 commercial presence and national treatment for service suppliers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and Regulations thereunder; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1 (proceeds of crime); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 24; United Nations Act, SC 1992, c 32; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp), ss 245 and 253; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 as amended by the Budget Implementation Act, 2023 (public corporate beneficial ownership registry). Provincial: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, including ULC provisions (s 15.1), registered office (s 17), registered records office (s 17.1), Individual with Significant Control (ISC) register (ss 20.1-20.3), and director residency rules; Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2022 (SA 2022, c 5); Business Names Registration Act, RSA 2000, c B-8; Alberta Corporate Registry fee schedule and Service Alberta registry policy. Regulatory guidance: FINTRAC Guidance on politically exposed persons and beneficial ownership; CRA guidance on permanent establishment and carrying on business.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (Alberta ISC register accessible to the Registrar, law enforcement, CRA, and prescribed authorities; transition to Fully_Public access expected under the federal corporate registry backstop regime effective for provincial registries in 2024-2025)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the founder's passport (identity verification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the designated Competent Authority of the issuing state (Canada has been a contracting state since January 14, 2024; China since November 7, 2023); no consular legalization required for Hague contracting states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter and proof of residential address for each founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution holding the shareholder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, where the issuing jurisdiction is not a Hague contracting state, Consular Legalization through Global Affairs Canada and the relevant consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Existence of the corporate shareholder (where the ULC shareholder is a US, EU, or PRC holding entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Secretary of State (US state), Companies House (UK), or equivalent national registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the issuing authority's designated Competent Authority; fallback Consular Legalization for non-Hague origin documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution of the parent entity authorizing incorporation of the Alberta ULC and designating the UBO and initial directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary for the parent entity's board of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (principal route for US/EU/China/Hague states); Consular Legalization fallback for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT pre-filing UBO and sanctions screening report (PEP/OFAC/UN/FINTRAC status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Canadian corporate service provider or Alberta legal counsel acting as the compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private_Internal (retained in the AML/CFT compliance file; notarization not required; screening updates every 90 days or upon material change)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and verification of every director, officer, promoter, and each individual with 25%% or more ownership or control interest against: (i) FINTRAC PEP/HIO definitions under PCMLTFA s 9.3 and Regulations; (ii) the UN Consolidated List and Canadian sanctions schedules under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (iii) the US OFAC SDN/Consolidated List for US-connected founders and for entities using USD payment rails; and (iv) Alberta corporate registry disqualification and bankruptcy checks. For a Low_Risk_Standard specialty tea lounge, simplified customer due diligence is available but does not exempt the service provider from identity verification, UBO identification, or ongoing monitoring. Enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, is mandatory upon any PEP, HIO, sanctions, adverse-media, or opacity trigger, and before acceptance of any subscription funds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - Corporate Access and Registry Search portals operated by Service Alberta; NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report must be obtained through an authorized service provider before filing Articles of Incorporation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin-script characters acceptable to the NUANS search algorithm; Alberta registry practice requires an English (or French) form of the corporate name; transliteration of a non-Latin script must be submitted in the English alphabet; no characters outside the standard English/French alphabet are permitted in the legal corporate name. The legal element for an Alberta unlimited liability corporation must be 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' (or the corresponding French form). A business trade name in another script may be registered separately under the Business Names Registration Act after incorporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects the proposed name (non-distinctive, confusingly similar, prohibited token, or misleading), the applicant must: (1) obtain a fresh NUANS report (valid 90 days) and either refile Articles of Incorporation with a revised name or file a Name Reservation/Amendment request; (2) where the objection relates to a confusingly similar trademark, obtain a written consent from the trademark owner or a court order; (3) apply to the Registrar under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) for reconsideration or correction within 30 days of the refusal; and (4) if still refused, seek judicial review by filing an originating application in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act, RSA 2000, c A-3 and the Alberta Rules of Court, Alta Reg 124/2010, Part 53, within the applicable limitation period (normally 30 days from the final administrative decision). Statutory name-reservation extension is not generally available; a fresh NUANS reservation is required after 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. The Business Corporations Act (Alberta) requires a registered office in Alberta for service of process and a registered records office in Alberta where corporate and ISC registers are kept; a post-office box is not acceptable. A virtual registered-office address operated by a licensed Alberta registered agent satisfies the statutory address requirement. However, the operating specialty tea salon and beverage-serving lounge must maintain an actual physical business premise in Alberta to obtain the Alberta Health Services food-service permit and the municipal business licence; a virtual office alone will not satisfy municipal, AHS, or Canada Revenue Agency commercial-substance expectations for the operating entity, and non-resident owners should note the ABCA requirement of at least one director resident in Canada for the ULC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: registry-level unannounced inspection of corporate books below 5%% for a private, non-distributing ULC; operational unannounced inspection risk of 25-40%% in year one through Alberta Health Services food-premises inspections (mandatory for beverage-serving establishments); Canada Revenue Agency audit or records-substance review risk of 3-7%% over the first three years for a low-risk, cash-light, POS-rail business.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search report and name clearance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Service Alberta Corporate Registry (via authorized NUANS service provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: CAD 40 registry fee plus service provider fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation filing fee for the Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Service Alberta corporate registry fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and registered records office service, first year (acceptance of service, records custody, ISC register maintenance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Alberta registered agent / corporate service provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act, RSA 2000, c C-21, including the provisions governing companies with unlimited liability. An Alberta ULC is not incorporated under the Business Corporations Act. Confirm the applicable Act, prescribed forms, and current requirements with Alberta Corporate Registry before filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction; filings are submitted through an authorized Alberta registry agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation under the Companies Act, filed with the prescribed incorporation application and supporting documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No general statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. The ULC's shareholders have unlimited liability as provided by its governing statute. No statutory escrow deposit is generally required for incorporation; confirm any banking or transaction-specific requirements separately. The stated USD fee is an approximate conversion of the Alberta government filing fee of CAD 275 and is subject to exchange-rate changes; registry-agent service fees are additional.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation accept the subscriptions for the shares set out in the subscription records and issue those shares upon receipt of the subscription consideration. RESOLVED that the registered office be established at the Alberta address approved by the directors and recorded in the corporate records. RESOLVED that [name] be appointed President and [name] be appointed Secretary, each to hold office until a successor is appointed or the appointment is earlier terminated. RESOLVED that the officers are authorized to complete post-incorporation filings, establish corporate banking arrangements, and take actions necessary to implement these resolutions, subject to the Companies Act and the Corporation's articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the proposed company qualifies for incorporation as an Alberta ULC under the Companies Act and verify current prescribed forms. Obtain a NUANS report if using a non-numbered name; ensure the name includes the required corporate designation and complies with registry rules. A numbered name may be available subject to registry requirements.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal name or numbered-name request
Proposed registered office address in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or the entity type is not accepted, revise the name or proposed structure and obtain confirmation from the registry agent before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; submission through an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the prescribed Companies Act incorporation forms and articles accurately. Submit them and the applicable fee through the registry agent. Foreign-executed documents may require notarization, authentication, or certified translations where required by the registry or the document's place of execution; confirm before submission. Do not assume notarization is routinely required for Alberta-signed forms.
required_dossiers: Executed articles of incorporation and prescribed application
Filing fee and registry-agent service fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address the registry's deficiency notice by correcting or supplementing the filing through the registry agent. If the application is refused, obtain written reasons and refile with corrected documents or seek legal advice on review options.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organize the corporation and maintain records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's directors and registered office; Alberta Corporate Registry for required notices and filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the certificate, hold the organizational directors' meeting or execute written resolutions. Approve share subscriptions and issuances, appoint officers, adopt the registered office, authorize banking, and establish the corporate records. File required changes to registered office, directors, or other registrable information within applicable statutory deadlines. Maintain ULC status and advise shareholders of unlimited liability.
required_dossiers: Subscription agreements and evidence of consideration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete corporate records promptly and submit any overdue statutory notice or filing. Obtain legal advice before issuing shares or operating if the articles, shareholder terms, or ULC liability consequences are unclear.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax and employer accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance and applicable employment authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA business number and register for GST/HST when required, payroll deductions before making payroll remittances, and other applicable program accounts. Assess Alberta corporate income tax and any non-resident ownership or cross-border tax consequences separately; ULC classification for foreign tax purposes is not guaranteed.
required_dossiers: Expected sales, payroll, and business commencement information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registration information through the relevant authority and file required returns or remittances. Seek cross-border tax advice before relying on pass-through treatment in another jurisdiction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality where the premises are located; Alberta Health Services Environmental Public Health
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before leasing, construction, or opening, confirm zoning and permitted use, obtain the municipal business licence and required development or building approvals, and contact Alberta Health Services about food-premises notification, plan review, inspection, and food-safety requirements. Requirements and timelines depend on the municipality, premises, menu, and service model.
required_dossiers: Development, building, and fire approvals as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to plan-review or inspection deficiencies with revised plans, corrective work, and reinspection. Do not commence regulated food operations until required approvals are obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No province-wide industrial licensing board generally licenses a tea salon. The relevant authorities are the municipality for business, zoning, building, and fire approvals, and Alberta Health Services Environmental Public Health for food-premises oversight. Additional approvals depend on location and activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal business licence (official title varies by municipality); food-premises notification, approval, or permit requirements administered by Alberta Health Services as applicable. A liquor licence from the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission is required if liquor is sold or served.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally no project-level EIA is expected for an ordinary tea salon in existing commercial premises. Environmental assessment or approvals may apply if the project falls within a designated activity or includes regulated emissions, wastewater, or waste operations; confirm with the agency and municipality.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with applicable municipal wastewater and sewer-use bylaws, including restrictions on fats, oils, solids, and prohibited discharges. No tea-salon-specific provincial VOC threshold generally applies. Handle solid waste, recyclables, and any controlled or hazardous waste under applicable provincial and municipal requirements; obtain approvals if regulated equipment or discharges are introduced.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain applicable municipal building and occupancy approvals and fire inspection or clearance before opening. Confirm occupant load, exits, fire protection, and any structural or accessibility work with the municipality and qualified professionals. Comply with Alberta occupational health and safety requirements, including hazard assessment, training, sanitation, and incident reporting. Specific structural-load certification depends on the premises and proposed work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Federal tax authority with portal at canada.ca/cra and My Business Account for online services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian entities, including ULCs, obtain a Business Number (BN) upon incorporation filings with the Alberta Corporate Registry. GST/HST registration is procured separately through the CRA portal if annual taxable supplies exceed the threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under Canadian tax law; hybrid mismatch rules and specific elections under the Income Tax Act (ITA) may apply for cross-border transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registrants file GST/HST returns periodically via My Business Account; digital filing and supporting documentation required, though real-time API clearance is not mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada or services performed outside Canada qualify for zero-rated GST/HST treatment. Proof of export or offshore performance is required for specialty tea products and salon services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may conduct audits on export claims; fraudulent zero-rating results in penalties up to 50% of the GST/HST amount, interest, and potential reassessment or criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), Ottawa — the sole note-issuing authority and administrator of the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) payment-service provider register. Foreign-exchange administration is functionally distributed: the Minister of Finance (under the Currency Act and the Export and Import Permits Act), the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential supervision of Schedule I banks, FINTRAC for cross-border currency reporting and AML/ATF enforcement, and Payments Canada for clearing and settlement infrastructure (Lynx RTGS and the retail Automated Clearing Settlement System).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. The Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1952; no Canadian statute requires government approval to convert CAD, remit profits, pay dividends, or repay shareholder loans. The CAD is a free-floating G10 currency and settlement in central-bank money is available through Lynx. An Alberta ULC may repatriate dividends to a US parent without Bank of Canada authorization; the only fiscal constraints are Part XIII withholding tax under Income Tax Act s.212 (25% statutory rate; 5% under Article X of the Canada-US Tax Convention where the US shareholder owns at least 10% of the voting stock) and FINTRAC's reporting thresholds. The IRS check-the-box pass-through election for the ULC does not alter Canadian exchange-control treatment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation deadline on export or trade receipts. The ULC may retain receipts in USD, CNY, or any freely convertible currency. Practical obligations: (i) FINTRAC reporting of any single cross-border transfer or cash-bound movement of C$10,000 or more under PCMLTFA Part 2 (Form E677); (ii) six-year retention of vendor invoices, CBSA B3 customs entries, and remittance advices to evidence commercial substance; (iii) for a tea salon importing loose-leaf tea, CFIA import permits and phytosanitary certificates must reconcile with amounts cleared through the bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD + USD multi-currency) / Capital Subscription Escrow (optional)
Operational Account (CAD + USD) / Capital Escrow Account for committed paid-in capital
Operational Account (CAD + USD) / Cross-border USD clearing via BMO Harris Bank
Operational Account (CAD + USD) / Trade Finance LC facility
Operational Account (CAD + USD) / Treasury FX forward line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: B+ (Medium) — permissible as auxiliary settlement rails; prohibited as the primary commercial banking relationship. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), non-bank payment service providers (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, and Canadian-registered MSBs) must register with the Bank of Canada; they are not banks under the Bank Act, offer no CDIC deposit insurance, lack direct access to Lynx RTGS, and cannot settle in central-bank money. For a tea salon importing loose-leaf tea (typical monthly supplier flows of C$5,000–80,000), an EMI business account may reduce CAD/CNY FX spreads by 35–90 basis points versus the Schedule I banks, but: (i) any balance held is an unsecured claim on the EMI; (ii) FINTRAC reporting is triggered at the primary bank for any cross-border flow of C$10,000 or more routed to an EMI; (iii) the ULC should cap EMI throughput at 20% of annual treasury flows and never route US-parent capital subscriptions or tax-related remittances through an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statute mandates an in-person banking visit: FINTRAC permits identity verification by technological means where the bank's AML risk model supports it under the PCMLTFA Part 1 regulatory framework. In practice, Schedule I banks require a physical 'new-to-bank' interview for any corporate client with non-resident ownership, which is the standard ULC profile. Banks generally insist on a Calgary or Edmonton branch appointment for the authorized director and any 25% or greater UBO; non-resident UBOs may rely on an apostilled or notarized board resolution, W-8BEN-E, IRS Form 8832 election, and a Canadian counsel introduction letter. Video onboarding is usually reserved for Canadian-resident signatories. Recommended procedure: execute a single branch-closing at the Alberta point of service with original certificates, corporate seal, and valid identification for all signing officers; thereafter conduct treasury operations exclusively through the bank's business portal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident (US) parent control combined with 'Unlimited Liability' designation — bank flags potential foreign-directed diversion and enhanced UBO watch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (1) Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate of Status issued within 30 days; (2) register of directors and members showing the full UBO chain; (3) IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election demonstrating US tax transparency; (4) W-8BEN-E of the ULC; (5) board resolution identifying the new banking mandate; (6) Canadian counsel's legal opinion confirming the unlimited-liability characterization is not an evasion mechanism under the Bank Act, PCMLTFA, or sanctions regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection — USD wire from the US parent to subscribe for ULC shares creates source-of-funds ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed share-subscription agreement; parent board minutes authorizing the contribution; 90 days of parent bank statements evidencing accumulated profits; source-of-wealth statutory declaration executed by the parent CFO; written confirmation that funds will be held in the capital escrow or designated account until the Alberta Corporate Registry filing reflects the share issuance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring high-volume supplier remittances to China, India, and Japan for tea inventory — trade-nexus red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreement; pro-forma invoices; CBSA B3 customs entry records; CFIA import permits; phytosanitary certificates; tea-broker reconciliation memo; stand-by use of irrevocable letters of credit for orders of USD 5,000 or more to evidence bona fide trade; after six months of clean trade history, request automated 'trade-cycle classification' downgrade to reduce monitoring intensity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive POS revenue — tea-salon cash deposits approaching or exceeding C$10,000 per day.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Daily POS Z-reads and merchant acquirer settlement reports (Moneris, Global Payments, or Elavon); internal cash-handling standard operating procedure; quarterly GIFI financial statements; express consent to the bank's automatic FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Report (LCTR); demonstrate that cash is deposited same-business-day and closing float is maintained at or below C$2,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated ULC (under 12 months) with no operating history and unlimited-liability articles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed leasehold agreement for the tea-salon premises; Alberta Health Services (AHS) food establishment permit; municipal business licence; 13-week cash-flow forecast and 24-month profit-and-loss projection prepared by a CPA; personal guarantee or parent-ULC comfort letter; CRA Business Number and GST/HST (RT) account activation confirmations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the US-parent contribution via SWIFT MT103 to the ULC's USD-denominated account at the chosen Alberta Schedule I bank. Field 70 must state 'ULC share subscription — [share class]/[certificate number] — [shareholder name]' and Field 72 should carry the ULC's CRA Business Number; the bank will verify the transfer against the CRS/FATCA W-8BEN-E and the UBO register, then convert into CAD at the in-branch treasury desk spot rate (reference: Bank of Canada daily rate). For structures requiring an escrow, freeze funds in a dedicated zero-interest Capital Escrow Account until (i) the Alberta Corporate Registry filing confirms the issuance, (ii) the bank receives the directors' certificate, and (iii) the ULC board authorizes release. Reporting purpose code: 'Business investment — equity injection'; no Bank of Canada approval, exchange permit, or ministerial authorization is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Tea-salon trade payables clear through three rails: (1) Domestic CAD operating expenses (rent, wages, POS merchant settlement) — Interac EFT and credit-clearing via Payments Canada at T+1; (2) Small foreign tea invoices under USD 5,000 — direct SWIFT MT103 remittance from the ULC's CAD operating account, with the bank converting at the 09:00 ET desk rate; (3) Bulk tea and ceramic crockery shipments of USD 5,000 or more — irrevocable at-sight commercial letter of credit issued by the bank's trade desk via SWIFT MT700, settled against an ocean bill of lading, commercial invoice, and packing list. The CAD leg settles through Lynx (RTGS) and the USD/CNY leg through the correspondent banking network; every documentary collection requires the CBSA B3 entry and CFIA import permit to evidence commercial substance. CNY supplier payments may be executed in offshore CNH through the bank's China desk upon presentation of the LC and related transport documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD/USD deliverable FX forwards (tenor up to 24 months; ISDA 2002 collateralized confirmations).
CAD/CNH deliverable forwards covering confirmed tea-import invoices (customarily 12 months or less).
Non-deliverable RMB (CNH) forward — permitted because Canada maintains no exchange controls; referenced to the CNH fixing where underlying settlement cannot be executed in CNY.
Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) for balance-sheet hedging of the parent loan or subscription receivable, with IFRS 9 hedge-accounting documentation.
FX option collars are permissible but discouraged for a small ULC without an express board derivatives mandate; speculative positions are prohibited by the bank's treasury code.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Corporate Registry Renewal and UBO Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 days after the corporation's registration anniversary date (annual maintenance date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No immediate flat fine, but the corporation is marked non-compliant; a continuing delinquency of 12 or more months exposes the ULC to administrative dissolution (strike-off) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). Reinstatement, if available, requires payment of prescribed reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of the taxation year; for a typical calendar-year tea lounge, by June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% for each full month of delay (up to 12 months), and arrears interest on any unpaid balance. A nil T2 must still be filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private, non-distributing Alberta ULC may waive an independent audit by unanimous shareholder resolution. A statutory audit becomes mandatory if the corporation is a distributing corporation or if shareholders holding at least five percent (5%) of the issued voting shares requisition an audit. There are no asset-revenue dollar thresholds for private ULCs under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (for public accountable enterprises); private non-distributing ULCs may elect Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises), both of which are accepted under the Alberta corporate and tax compliance framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual return, the ULC must confirm that its Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO register) is complete and accurate and must update the register within 30 days of any share transfer that changes significant beneficial ownership.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 7,500 per engagement (if an audit is required or requisitioned)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined federal-provincial general corporate rate (15% federal Part I under s. 123 ITA + 8% Alberta general rate effective 1 January 2020); 11% combined small business rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta) unavailable because a non-resident-controlled ULC is not a CCPC
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral tax holiday applies to ISIC 5630 food-service income in Alberta; federal General Rate Reduction (s. 123.4) lowers the basic 28% federal rate to 15%; SR&ED 35% refundable/15% non-refundable ITC is generally not applicable to tea salon operations; Alberta offers no general corporate tax holiday, and municipal business tax levies may apply

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 – Corporation Income Tax Return, filed via the CRA's Corporation Internet Filing / XML service using certified tax preparation software; Alberta corporate tax is assessed on the same T2 under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act and collected by the CRA
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual – each taxation year (typically 12 months, may be a short fiscal period up to 53 weeks); installments are due quarterly (monthly for larger CCPCs) under s. 157 ITA
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 6 months after fiscal year-end (s. 150(1) ITA); payment of any balance-due is due within 2 months after year-end for a non-CCPC ULC (s. 157(1)); 3 months applies only to CCPCs with taxable capital below CAD 15 million

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Page 1 – Identification block (Box 1: Business Number, Box 2: Legal name)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the ULC's 15-digit CRA Business Number (RC program account), legal name as registered with Alberta Corporate Registries, registered office address in Alberta, and the month of the taxation year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A ULC controlled by non-residents uses the Alberta registered office as the mailing address; the T2 must disclose each non-resident director's country of residence and the corporation's foreign ownership percentage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable income computed under s. 3 ITA after claiming non-capital loss carryforwards (Schedule 4), capital cost allowance (Schedule 8/Class 1 leasehold improvements), and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable income is limited to Canadian-source business income attributable to the Alberta permanent establishment; non-resident shareholders' foreign losses cannot be applied unless a valid s. 216.3(1) ULC flow-through election makes the entity a partnership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Page 3 – Line 300 and Line 330: Federal tax before credits and General Rate Reduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base Part I tax at 38%, less 10% provincial abatement and 13% GRR, yielding 15% federal tax on general taxable income; add refundable taxes (Part IV dividend tax where applicable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 10% abatement (s. 124) is allowed only for income allocated to a Canadian province; verify the Alberta allocation on T2 Schedule 5 using gross revenue and salary/wages factors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute Alberta tax at 8% on taxable income allocated to Alberta using T2 Schedule 5 apportionment; Alberta does not permit a small business deduction for a non-resident-controlled ULC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Alberta allocation percentage is based on the average of the Alberta gross revenue ratio and Alberta salary/wages ratio to the nationwide totals; no separate Alberta return is filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Page 4 – Line 580: Total tax payable and Line 660/670: Remittance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Combine federal and Alberta tax, apply foreign tax credits and investment tax credits, subtract installments, and report the balance due (Line 660) or overpayment (Line 670).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remit the balance-due electronically via CRA My Payment to the RC account within 2 months of year-end; late payment accrues interest at the prescribed rate (s. 161) compounded daily.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T106 – Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose every reportable transaction with a non-resident related person (purchases, royalties, management fees, intercompany debt) including currency amounts and pricing method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File T106 with the T2 and maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation under s. 247(4); failure to file T106 may trigger a CAD 2,500 penalty (12-month period) plus additional per-transaction penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: s. 162(1) ITA – 5% of the unpaid balance due on the filing deadline plus 1% per full month of delay (maximum 12 months); where no tax is payable, a minimum CAD 100 penalty applies; second offense within 3 years: 10% plus 2% per month (max 20%). Late/insufficient installments and balance-due: prescribed-rate interest (currently approx. 7%–9% per year, compounded daily). Alberta's penalty regime is administered through the same T2 assessment; willful failure may be prosecuted under s. 239 (fine of 50%–200% of evaded tax and up to 2 years' imprisonment).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding under s. 212(2) ITA on dividends paid by the Alberta-resident ULC to a non-resident shareholder; no exemption for management companies; refundable to the recipient only via treaty or NR7-R claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Canada–U.S. Convention (Fifth Protocol), Art. X: 5% on direct dividends where the beneficial owner is a U.S. company owning at least 10% of the ULC's voting stock; 15% for portfolio dividends; all relief subject to Art. XXIX A (Limitation on Benefits). Protocol: (1) the U.S. shareholder completes Form NR302 – Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Treaty – and delivers it to the ULC before each dividend payment; (2) obtain a U.S. Certificate of Residency (TRC) from the IRS via Form 8802/Form 6166 when the Canadian payer or the CRA demands corroboration; (3) the ULC withholds at the applicable treaty rate at source; (4) if 25% was withheld in error, the shareholder files Form NR7-R with the CRA within 2 years for a refund; (5) retain NR302 and the TRC for six years to support the audit trail.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% under s. 212(1)(d) ITA on payments for the use of IP (tea brand, recipes, software); Canada–U.S. treaty rate 10% for most industrial/commercial royalties (Art. XII), 0% only for certain film/literary copyrights. Interest: statutory 25% under s. 212(1)(b) ITA on arm's-length and related-party debt; Canada–U.S. treaty rate 0% for most arm's-length interest (Art. XI), 15% for participating/contingent-interest debt; the thin-capitalization rule (s. 18(4)) disallows interest on debt beyond a 1.5:1 debt-to-equity ratio owed to 25%+ non-resident shareholders.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory CAD threshold for preparing a T2 transfer-pricing file; however, under s. 247(4) ITA a participant must produce documentation within 3 months of a CRA written demand to avoid the 10% penalty. The CRA's administrative audit expectation is that contemporaneous transparency sets exist where aggregate non-arm's length cross-border transactions exceed approximately CAD 1,000,000 annually; OECD Country-by-Country filing (Form RC4649) applies only to a Canadian-headquartered group with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000.
